quote: Our findings delineate a novel epithelial FPR1/NOX1-dependent redox signaling pathway that promotes mucosal wound repair.
summary: An epithelial FPR1/NOX1 signalling pathway activated by annexin A1 promotes epithelial migration and mucosal wound repair in mice; the in vivo knockouts were of Nox1 and AnxA1, not FPR1.

quote: Using a similar approach, ALX/FPR1 heterodimerization evoked using the panagonist peptide Ac2-26, identified a JNK-mediated proapoptotic path that was confirmed in primary neutrophils.
summary: FPR1 heterodimerised with FPR2/ALX and, on agonist Ac2-26, triggered a JNK-mediated proapoptotic pathway in neutrophils; no colitis outcome.

quote: How these chemically diverse ligands are recognized by the three human FPRs (FPR1, FPR2 and FPR3) and their murine equivalents is largely unclear.
summary: Review of ligand diversity and recognition by formyl peptide receptors including FPR1; no UC data.

quote: In this review, we explore the multiple components of neutrophil migration and function in both health and disease, with a focus on the role of FPR1 in these processes.
summary: Review of FPR1 in neutrophil migration and function in inflammatory disease, concluding it is a key regulator of the inflammatory environment.
FMLP is the peptide stimulus in neutrophil assays of pentoxifylline, not the FPR1 gene.
FPR1 here is the yeast FK506-binding proline rotamase gene, not the human formyl peptide receptor.

quote: Our results demonstrate that formyl peptide receptor 1 (FPR1) and neutrophilic NADPH oxidase (NOX2) are required for the rapid depletion of microenvironmental oxygen and compensatory responses, resulting in a dramatic enrichment of an anaerobic bacterial consortium.
summary: In mouse colonic wounds, FPR1 was required for a pro-restitutive microbiota response and for Akkermansia-stimulated enterocyte proliferation and migration.
FMLP is used only as a chemotactic stimulus for neutrophil transmigration across epithelial monolayers, not as the FPR1 gene.

quote: Stimulation of the formyl peptide receptor (FPR) led to ATP release through pannexin-1 (panx1) hemichannels, and FPRs colocalized with P2Y2 nucleotide receptors on the cell surface to form a purinergic signaling system that facilitated neutrophil activation.
summary: FPR stimulation drives ATP release and purinergic signalling in neutrophils; the perturbed genes were panx1 and P2Y2, not FPR1, and there is no UC data.
fMLP appears only as a bacterial product whose flux across the claudin-7-deficient epithelium was measured, not as the FPR1 gene.

quote: The mechanism whereby this protein exerts its effects is likely to be through the FPR receptor family-a hitherto rather enigmatic family of G protein coupled receptors, which are increasingly implicated in the regulation of many inflammatory processes.
summary: Review of annexin A1 in immune regulation that proposes FPR family receptors mediate its actions; no FPR1-specific data.
fMLP is the peptide transported by hPepT1 in colonic cells, not the FPR1 gene.

quote: Consequently, after infection, mice deficient in Fpr1 display increased microbial translocation, poor commensal containment, and increased mortality.
summary: Fpr1-deficient mice infected with Toxoplasma had poor containment of commensals, more microbial translocation and higher mortality, indicating a protective role.
FMLP is the neutrophil stimulus in a study of an NADPH oxidase inhibitor, not the FPR1 gene.

quote: Taken together, these findings identify a novel role of FPR1 as pattern recognition receptors for perceiving the enteric microbiota that promotes repair of mucosal wounds via generation of reactive oxygen species from the enterocyte NOX1.
summary: Commensal bacteria stimulate FPR1 on intestinal epithelial cells to drive NOX1 ROS, migration and proliferation that repair colonic wounds.
fMLP is only the chemotactic stimulus in an osteopontin neutrophil study, not the FPR1 gene.

quote: Three FPRs have been identified in human: FPR1-FPR3, with putative corresponding mouse counterparts.
summary: Review of formyl peptide receptors including FPR1 in leukocyte trafficking, tissue repair and inflammation-associated tumorigenesis.
FMLP is listed only as a chemoattractant peptide that induces experimental colitis, not as the FPR1 gene.
The study concerns FPR2/ALX in atherosclerosis, a different receptor from FPR1.
FMLP is used as a phagocyte stimulus in colonic electrolyte transport experiments, not as the FPR1 gene.

quote: ROS generation induced by the commensal bacteria Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG and the FPR peptide ligand, N-formyl-Met-Leu-Phe, was abolished in the presence of selective inhibitors for G protein-coupled signaling and FPR ligand interaction.
summary: Inhibiting FPR ligand interaction blocked commensal-induced ROS and ERK signalling in intestinal epithelial cells; no inflammation or colitis outcome was measured.
fMLP is a comparator chemoattractant in a CXC chemokine neutrophil rolling study, not the FPR1 gene.
FMLP is the peptide stimulus in an H. pylori neutrophil study, not the FPR1 gene.

quote: In the dextran sulfate sodium-induced colitis inflammation model, CXCL2 expression, neutrophil infiltration and ulceration were attenuated by Trpm2 disruption.
summary: CXCL2 expression in DSS colitis fell with Trpm2 disruption; CXCL2 was a downstream readout and was not itself perturbed.

quote: This paper reviews all available information on hypoxia-induced changes in the expression of all CXC chemokines (CXCL1, CXCL2, CXCL3, CXCL4, CXCL5, CXCL6, CXCL7, CXCL8 (IL-8), CXCL9, CXCL10, CXCL11, CXCL12 (SDF-1), CXCL13, CXCL14, CXCL15, CXCL16, CXCL17) as well as CXC chemokine receptors-CXCR1, CXCR2, CXCR3, CXCR4, CXCR5, CXCR6, CXCR7 and CXCR8.
summary: Review of hypoxia effects on CXC chemokines including CXCL2 in cancer; no UC content.
